name: Sosaties
summary: Curried lamb and apricot kebabs: lamb marinated in a sweet-sour curry sauce, threaded with dried apricots and onion and charred on the braai.
about: Sosaties come from the Cape Malay kitchen; the name joins sate, skewered meat, and saus, a spicy sauce. The lamb is marinated overnight or longer in a sweet-sour curry sauce, then threaded with dried apricots and onion and cooked over coals — a fixture of South African braais.

ingredients.name: Lamb leg or shoulder
ingredients.note: boned, cut into 3 cm cubes, a little fat left on

ingredients.name: Onions
ingredients.note: cut into wedges and separated into layers

ingredients.name: Skewers
ingredients.note: wooden ones soaked in water for 30 minutes

steps: Heat the oil in a saucepan over medium heat and fry the chopped onion until soft and golden, 6–8 minutes. Add the garlic, curry powder, turmeric and coriander and stir for 1 minute.
Add the jam, vinegar, sugar, bay leaves and salt and simmer for 5 minutes, until slightly syrupy. Leave to cool completely, about 20 minutes.
Put the lamb in a glass or ceramic bowl, pour over the cooled marinade and mix well. Cover and refrigerate for 24 hours (at least overnight, up to 2 days), turning the meat once or twice.
When you are ready to cook, soak the apricots in hot water for 15 minutes and drain. Thread the lamb onto the skewers, alternating with apricots and pieces of onion.
Pour the leftover marinade into a small pot and boil it for 3–4 minutes; use it for basting and as a sauce.

Braai over medium-hot coals (you can hold your hand above the grid for 5–6 seconds) for 12–15 minutes, turning every 3 minutes and basting in the last 5, until charred at the edges and just pink in the middle. Cook a few minutes longer if you prefer it well done.
Rest for 5 minutes. Serve with yellow rice and the warm sauce.
prepNote: Marinate the lamb 1–2 days ahead; the flavour gets better.
